text:
maya: quick RFC follow-up — we need to pick a v2 surface for service auth. current options: long-lived API keys per project, short-lived service tokens with delegated scopes, or a hybrid where infra issues short-lived tokens on behalf of service-accounts. tradeoffs: operator UX, rotation, auditability, and cross-project calls. thoughts?
liam: prefer short-lived tokens issued by an auth service. simpler to rotate and revoke. also lets us attach per-request metadata for tracing. downside: more runtime calls and complexity in infra.
olga: agree on short-lived, but we should avoid a synchronous blocking call on every request. propose caching tokens per instance with small TTL + automatic refresh + circuit breaker.
maya: +1 on caching. also need to decide on identity model: are service accounts first-class (global) or always project-scoped? global svc-accounts simplify cross-project flows but widen blast radius.
sam: product/security perspective: default to project-scoped tokens for new services; allow explicit opt-in to cross-project service accounts with owners and justification. that helps compliance.
liam: for opt-in cross-project, we should require an admin-approved role binding and record the justification in audit log. implement via a "delegation" resource in control plane.
maya: about RBAC rules — do we keep coarse role names (reader/writer/admin) or support resource-level permissions (e.g., model.deploy, dataset.read)? more expressive is better but harder to manage at scale.
olga: recommend hybrid: coarse roles for most teams + fine-grained roles for platform infra and security-sensitive workflows. expose templates to reduce ACL sprawl.
sam: token format idea: short-lived JWT with claims {iss, sub, aud, scope, exp, jti, origin_project}. store jti in revocation index for immediate revokes. when cross-project, include delegated_by claim.
maya: sample token issuance flow CLI snippet for reference:
```
# request a token for svc-account
curl -X POST https://auth.redwood.example/v2/issue \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $CLI_API_KEY" \
  -d '{"svc_account":"svc/foo","scope":"model.deploy","ttl":300}'
```
liam: small UX ask: provide a brokered SDK that transparently fetches + refreshes tokens for SDK users — reduces adoption friction.
amaya: (typo) meant maya: +1 to SDK. also integrate with our existing service mesh mTLS so services inside VPC can use mTLS identity as extra signal.
olga: implementation note: avoid coupling auth service to datastore hot path. use async telemetry export for usage accounting; keep core token issuance path lean.
sam: regarding audit: every issuance, refresh, and revoke should be forwarded to SIEM with user/service, invoking_principal, reason, and request_metadata. retention policy depends on enterprise tier.
liam: migration plan: phase 1: new services use short-lived tokens; phase 2: existing long-lived keys get a TTL and rotation window; phase 3: forcibly rotate and revoke older keys. need a migration tool to bulk-map service principals to new svc-accounts.
maya: open question: do we allow impersonation APIs (service A acts-as service B) for workflow chaining? secure but dangerous. suggestion: allow only with explicit delegation tokens and admin grants, record both principals in audit.
sam: +1 on restricted impersonation; require 2FA or owner approval for delegation grant.
auth-bot: deploy-bot: noted. filed infra ticket INFRA-1134 to prototype token broker and TTL cache.
liam: next steps: I'll draft a lightweight RFC with diagrams and perf targets. olga, can you sketch the cache + circuit-breaker numbers?
olga: will do. initial numbers: cache TTL 30s, refresh jitter 5s, circuit open after 3 consecutive failures per instance, backoff 60s.
maya: thanks all — let's keep thread for follow-ups. :thumbsup:
